title: Epochal compact scheduler with KV thermal prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Continuous batching at high GPU utilization leads to two failure modes: (1) large tenants monopolize KV residency causing long-tail latency regressions for small low-latency tenants, and (2) on-demand preemption that naively evicts large KV working sets causes spikes and transient QoS drops. Goal: introduce a preemption/fairness policy that minimizes 99/99.9 latency regressions while keeping aggregate throughput high and avoiding full-device pauses.

Proposed approach: Epochal Compact Scheduler with KV Thermal Prioritization
- Epochal compaction: instead of immediate global evictions on pressure, the scheduler performs short, frequent compaction epochs (50-200ms windows) where small slices of memory are reclaimed from candidates. Each epoch interleaves with normal batching so no single epoch stops the serving pipeline.
- KV Thermal Prioritization: compute a lightweight per-tenant KV "thermal" score combining recency, access-rate, and resident-size. Thermal = alpha * recency_score + beta * access_rate_norm + gamma * size_penalty. Lower thermal => colder => higher eviction candidate. Recency decays exponentially with half-life tuned per model family.
- Reservationless small-slot reclaim: avoid hard reservations or large token-budget withdrawals. When an epoch runs, reclaim is proportional to KV cold mass and tenant SLO slack (latency headroom). Tenants with tight SLOs get softer reclaim weights.
- Diffuse preemption: reclaimed resources are returned to the global pool and used immediately by admitted batches; the algorithm prefers to reclaim from tenants with sustained coldness across multiple epochs to avoid oscillation.

Architecture/Integration points:
- Runtime: add "compaction epochs" scheduler hook in the serving loop (configurable frequency). Integrate with KV cache metadata (per-tenant access histograms, resident size counters). Keep per-device compaction token bucket to bound compaction work.
- Admission controller: use SLO slack signal from routing layer (percentile headroom over target) to bias reclaim weights. If a tenant is already meeting SLOs by a margin, it becomes a candidate sooner.
- Metrics & observability: new metrics: kv_thermal_score_{tenant}, compact_epoch_duration, bytes_reclaimed_per_epoch, reclaim_success_ratio, slo_slack_estimate. Dashboards: per-tenant heatmap and epoch timeline.

Rollout plan:
1) Simulation: run workload replay with production traces (7 days) in the simulator; validate 99/99.9 latency and throughput.
2) Canary-on-hosted: enable epochal compact on 5% of traffic with metric gating.
3) Canary-on-dedicated: run on a dedicated pool with mixed tenants; evaluate cross-tenant fairness.
4) Gradual ramp with automatic rollback on regressions.

Success criteria:
- 99th and 99.9th latency for low-latency tenants improves or stays within a 5% delta versus baseline under mixed load.
- Aggregate token throughput decreases by <3% at steady state.
- KV eviction churn is reduced (measured as fewer full working-set evictions and lower bytes_reclaimed_per_minute).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: mis-tuned thermal weights could starve large high-throughput tenants -> mitigation: conservative default weights and per-tenant override via placement policies.
- Risk: compaction epochs introduce overhead -> mitigation: token-bucket throttle and ability to disable epochs on high CPU pressure.
- Risk: SLO slack signal noise -> mitigation: smooth slack over sliding window and ignore transient spikes.

Open design questions:
- Optimal epoch length (50ms vs 200ms) across GPU families. Plan: microbench across rtx-80xx and a100 variants.
- Decay half-life for recency_score per model family.
- Whether to include inter-tenant fairness floor (hard minimum kv-residency).

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/epochal-compact-scheduler (draft)
- Simulator repo (workload replay): https://github.com/redwood-inference/compact-sim/pull/47
- Initial implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2184
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-thermal/epochal-compact-ops

Next steps:
- Finish simulator runs (ETA 2025-02-14) and attach results to this ticket.
- Iterate on thermal coefficients with ML/metrics to find conservative defaults.
- Implement per-device token bucket in runtime and add gating flags for canary rollout.
comments: 2025-02-05 - Marco Ruiz: Initial spike simulation looks promising. With alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=0.1 our simulated 99.9th latency for small tenants dropped 18% at 85% GPU util. Need more run coverage across models.
2025-02-10 - Janelle Kim (PM): Good direction. Please add acceptance criteria for canary (gating thresholds for rollback). Also list any customer-facing changes.
2025-02-12 - Marco Ruiz: Added gating thresholds: if 99th latency for any tier increases >10% for 5 consecutive minutes during canary, auto-disable. Pushed simulator artifacts to the repo.

2025-02-18 - Ethan Zhou (Eng reviewer): Reviewed PR #2184. Major feedback: compact epoch must avoid allocator lock contention; switched to lock-free per-shard reclaim snapshots. See review comments on the PR.

2025-03-01 - Marco Ruiz: Canary started on hosted 5% traffic. Early telemetry: bytes_reclaimed_per_epoch stable, reclaim_success_ratio 0.88. Observed a single transient spike correlated with GC in python model runner; investigating.
2025-03-06 - Priya Menon (SRE): Observed increased CPU on control-plane when epochs at 200ms. Recommendation: start at 100ms default and enable adaptive backoff when CPU > 65%.
2025-03-07 - Marco Ruiz: Updated default epoch to 100ms and added token-bucket cap of 16KB reclaimed per-epoch per-device. Scheduling follow-up for per-model family tuning (ENG-45967).
